If sentiment is negative (≤0.0) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for early horizon (1–7 days) to correct over-optimism.

If sentiment is positive (≥0.67) and forecast peaks > 75% above recent 18-day average, cap forecast at 10% below peak for mid horizon (8–15 days) to prevent overcorrection.

If sentiment is neutral (0.33) and forecast diverges > 2.0% from true path for 3+ consecutive days, apply linear regression correction to align with sentiment trend for late horizon (16–30 days).

If sentiment swings from positive to negative within 5 days, reduce forecast slope by 15–20% for early horizon to reflect sentiment reversal.

If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) and forecast remains >70% above true path, apply downward bias of 1.5–2.5% per day for late horizon to reflect bearish sentiment persistence.

If sentiment is high (≥0.67) and forecast is below true path by >1.5% for 3+ days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day for mid horizon to capture sentiment-driven rebound.
